content.value_statement: Metabolic modeling workflows can be hard to assemble from scattered COBRApy examples. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code focused guidance for common analyses.
actual_capabilities: Explains how to load, save, and inspect COBRApy models in SBML, JSON, and YAML formats.
Provides patterns for FBA, pFBA, geometric FBA, FVA, and production envelopes.
Guides gene deletion, reaction deletion, media design, gapfilling, and flux sampling workflows.
Shows how to build models with reactions, metabolites, bounds, objectives, and gene reaction rules.
Summarizes troubleshooting steps for infeasible, slow, or unbounded optimization results.
limitations: Does not install COBRApy or external solvers for the user.
Does not validate biological assumptions or curated model quality.
Examples require compatible model files and a working Python environment.
Large sampling and deletion studies may need significant compute resources.

use_cases.title: Run Growth Simulations
use_cases.description: Load a genome-scale model, run FBA, and inspect active pathways for a target condition.

use_cases.title: Design Production Strains
use_cases.description: Compare production envelopes, knockouts, and media changes for a desired metabolite.

use_cases.title: Teach COBRApy Workflows
use_cases.description: Use concise examples to explain model structure, flux constraints, and validation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Load and Optimize a Model
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me load a COBRApy model from SBML, run FBA, and explain the growth result step by step.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Flux Ranges
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through FVA for selected reactions, including fraction_of_optimum choices and how to interpret wide ranges.

prompt_templates.title: Screen Gene Knockouts
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a single gene deletion study for my model. Include result interpretation, essential gene thresholds, and common validation checks.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Production Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an advanced COBRApy workflow for target metabolite production. Include media constraints, production envelopes, knockout ranking, and loopless FVA.

output_examples.input: A user asks how to run FBA on an E. coli model.
output_examples.output: The response outlines model loading, optimization, status checks, objective value interpretation, and flux table review.

output_examples.input: A user asks for production strain design guidance.
output: A workflow compares baseline growth, target metabolite production, knockout candidates, and media constraints.
The result includes cautions about growth constraints, solver performance, and validation.

output_examples.input: A user has an infeasible model.
output_examples.output: The response lists checks for medium composition, reaction bounds, exchange reactions, mass balance, and solver status.

best_practices: Use context managers for temporary objective, bound, or knockout changes.
Check optimization status before interpreting objective values or fluxes.
Validate models and samples before drawing biological conclusions.
anti_patterns: Do not assume a feasible solution means the biology is correct.
Do not overwrite model media without reassigning the complete medium dictionary.
Do not run large deletion or sampling jobs without planning solver and CPU use.

faq.question: Does this skill run COBRApy automatically?
faq.answer: No. It guides analysis patterns and example workflows for use in your Python environment.

faq.question: Which file formats are covered?
faq.answer: It covers SBML, JSON, and YAML model loading and saving patterns.

faq.question: Can it help with gene knockout studies?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains single and double deletion workflows and result interpretation.

faq.question: Does it support metabolic engineering design?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers production envelopes, media constraints, gapfilling, and knockout prioritization.

faq.question: What tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: It is marked for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Are external solvers required?
faq.answer: Some workflows can use default solvers, but large or MILP tasks may need faster configured solvers.
